source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
List the location of the building, date and time of inspection, and the name(s) of the inspector(s).
3. For each failed check, clearly document the area or system that was checked and include relevant photos or diagrams.
4. Specify why the check failed; be descriptive and include any relevant codes, standards, or requirements not met.
5. Note if any corrective actions were recommended and the deadline for those actions to be completed.
6. Mention if the building occupants were informed of the failed inspection and the risks involved.
7. Include any relevant communication with building management regarding the failed checks, such as email or letter correspondence.
8. If applicable, record whether the failed items are considered critical violations and if they pose an immediate threat to safety.
9. Include the inspector’s signature or initials and the date of documentation.
10. File the report and retain copies for further reference or follow-up inspections.
